headline: SILVER SURGES 1.94% BACK TO $56.71 — PRECIOUS METALS FIND FOOTING AFTER CPI CRASH
snippet: Silver rebounded 1.94% to $56.71 per troy ounce on October 15, outpacing gold's flat session near $4,141 as precious metals stabilized following the prior session's CPI-driven crash that had sent silver down 6% to a three-month low of $55.41. Traders remain cautious with the October 27-28 Federal Reserve meeting as the next major catalyst for direction.

headline: SELKIRK COPPER DRILLS 44.7M AT 2.12% Cu IN YUKON — PHASE 2 BLOWS PAST 50,000M TARGET
snippet: Selkirk Copper (TSXV: SCMI) released hole 26SCM237 from its Phase 2 drill program at the Minto Project in Yukon, returning 44.7 metres at 2.12% copper, 1.16 g/t gold and 10.7 g/t silver (3.0% CuEq). By October 14, the program had exceeded its 50,000-metre Phase 2 target with further assays expected through fall and winter.

headline: TUDOR GOLD EXPANDS TREATY CREEK PERFECTSTORM ZONE — 96M AT 0.85 g/t Au IN LATEST FOUR HOLES
snippet: Tudor Gold (TSXV: TUD) reported four new holes from the Perfectstorm Zone at its Treaty Creek property in British Columbia's Golden Triangle, extending the copper-gold-silver-molybdenum porphyry system. Highlight hole PS-26-30 returned 0.85 g/t gold over 96.3 metres, growing a system that has driven significant re-rating during the 2026 drill season.

headline: NORTHWEST COPPER CUTS 31.4M AT 0.92% Cu AND 1.08 g/t Au AT KWANIKA PIT ZONE
snippet: NorthWest Copper (TSXV: NWST) released three new holes from the Pit Zone at its Kwanika copper-gold project in British Columbia, with highlight hole K-26-306 returning 31.4 metres grading 0.92% copper and 1.08 g/t gold from 78 metres depth. The results support an open-pit development pathway for a deposit growing toward a formal resource update.

headline: HYCROFT DRILLS 'BEST HOLE IN COMPANY HISTORY' — NEW RECORD INTERCEPT AT NEVADA GOLD-SILVER PROJECT
snippet: Hycroft Mining (Nasdaq: HYMC) reported that drill hole H26D-6175A returned the highest-grade intercept in company history at its Hycroft gold-silver project in Nevada, with CEO Casey Nault calling it an exceptional result. The result is part of the ongoing 2025-2026 Exploration Drill Program targeting depth extensions beneath the existing resource.

headline: GREAT PLAINS METALS STAGES GOODRICH FOLLOW-UP — STAGE 1 PORPHYRY DISCOVERY HOLE HIT CONTINUOUS 128M
snippet: Great Plains Metals (TSXV: GPS) announced a fully funded 1,000-metre Stage 2 diamond drill program at its Goodrich copper-gold project in New South Wales following a Stage 1 discovery hole that returned 128 continuous metres of porphyry-style mineralization at 0.47% CuEq. Stage 2 will test targets above, below and along strike of the discovery.

headline: MYRIAD URANIUM SNAPS UP 55,013-HECTARE LOS ALTARES IN ARGENTINA — C$1M DEAL ADDS PATAGONIA URANIUM ADDRESS
snippet: Myriad Uranium signed a definitive agreement to acquire Green Shift Commodities' Los Altares uranium project in Argentina on October 13 — 23 properties totalling 55,013 hectares — for C$300,000 cash, C$700,000 in Myriad shares and a 2% net smelter return royalty. Some properties already carry granted mining concessions, accelerating the company's Patagonian exploration timeline.

headline: COPPER RETREATS TO $6.53/LB AS MARKET ENTERS WAIT-AND-SEE MODE AHEAD OF OCT. 27-28 FED DECISION
snippet: Copper futures pulled back sharply on October 15 to $6.53 per pound (-1.16%), with Shanghai futures closing at 109,610 yuan per tonne, as secondary copper market activity dried up ahead of the October 27-28 Federal Reserve policy decision. The market has now fully retraced the rally driven by Escondida labor tension earlier in the week.

headline: 2 RARE EARTH STOCKS CUTTING CHINA'S GRIP — LYNAS BRAZIL PLANT ADVANCES AS WESTERN EX-CHINA SUPPLY BUILDS
snippet: An October 13 analysis spotlights two rare earth producers building meaningful non-Chinese supply chains, including Lynas Rare Earths advancing a Brazilian processing plant with state support. The piece argues investors willing to look past short-term US-China diplomatic warming can find structural positioning ahead of long-term Western critical mineral demand.

headline: 'ULTIMATE THEMATIC UNCHANGED' — EXPERT DEFENDS LITHIUM AND COPPER LONG CASE DESPITE 25% MONTHLY SELLOFF
snippet: Argonaut's research head argues that despite lithium carbonate spot prices falling 25% in a month and spodumene suffering similar losses in a seasonally weak period, the fundamental EV adoption and grid electrification demand curves remain intact. The analysis urges investors to separate short-term macro headwinds from the long-run structural deficit thesis underpinning lithium and copper juniors.
